item.title: The Ni No Kuni Universe Welcomes A New Crafting Adventure, And It's Heading To Switch

description.p: Bloomwalking into a familiar series.As part of yesterday's Xbox Tokyo Games Show event, Netmarble shared another look at Bloomwalker, its upcoming crafting adventure. Aside from announcing that the game will launch on Switch 1 & 2, the studio also revealed that the title is officially part of the Ni no Kuni universe.It has been a little while since we got a first peek at Bloomwalker, but it looks like it'll be right at home on Nintendo consoles. It's got all manner of cosiness that we love to see on the system, as you travel across a pollution-ravaged land with your moving house (yes really) and adorable nature spirit pals, and there's more than enough crafting that we can imagine portability will be a welcome addition.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Japanese Charts: Rhythm Heaven Groove Surpasses 1 Million Boxed Units Sold

description.p: It just keeps going.Famitsu has posted the latest data for boxed sales in Japan, and it's Rhythm Heaven Groove that takes the top spot once again. Not only that, but consistent sales have now put the Switch game at over 1 million total boxed sales in the region. Pretty neat.Onimusha: Way of the Sword is the next big success of the week, with PS5 sales totalling 19,654 and Switch 2 totalling 7,070. This means that combined sales actually put it above Rhythm Heaven Groove. Worldwide sales for the game topped 1 million in just a single day, so we're expecting Capcom to announce another major milestone any day now.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Feature: How Does Zelda: Ocarina Of Time's Old & New Art Compare? Here's A Side-By-Side Face-Off

description.p: Which do you prefer?It's almost been a week, and we're still thinking about that Ocarina of Time deep dive Direct. The new details are one thing (hello, Goggles of Truth!), but it's the visuals that are stuck in our minds. It all looks so shiny, so crisp, so... different.Of course, it's hardly a drastic departure — these are still very clearly the characters and locales that we all remember from the N64 — but still, the new look has been enough to leave us heading back to the original on NSO (or a swanky Analogue 3D, in some cases) just to really soak in the differences.Read the full article on nintendolife.com
